what: Stick sensitivity (the owner's item 7: 'the DJI feels much more sensitive than my previous radio'). How a stick reaches the physics: HID logical range -> -1..1 (DJI raw / 660 on WebHID and on the Gamepad API alike; EdgeTX (v - 1024) / 1024), then the profile's centre and ends, the deadband, then the rates (expo lives in the rates). The wizard took each stick's ends from the farthest it saw while setting up.
tool: tools/radios/sensitivity.ts (480 simulated people, packages/input/src/sim/human.ts: a model, not measured humans) and the owner's real DJI stir (packages/input/test/fixtures/dji-rc3-stir.ts)
metric: halfReading: what roll / pitch / yaw read at half the physical stick travel, the more sensitive direction (ideal 0.5; 0.55 = 10 % more sensitive). fullAtTravel: the share of the travel at which a stick already reads full (ideal 1). peopleAnyStickOver10pct: people with at least one stick more than 10 % too sensitive.

after.rule: TUNING.END_SNAP 0.85: a roll / pitch / yaw end seen at 85 % or more of the device scale is the full scale; the throttle keeps its ends (its bottom must read 0 % for the arm gate)

djiRealStir.note: the wizard sets each stick end to the farthest value seen; -1 and +1 = the full range, so this stir gives no extra sensitivity

findings: The DJI controller itself: the owner's real 25 s stir reached -660 and +660 on all four sticks, so a wizard run with a full stir gives it the full range: the calibration did not make the DJI more sensitive than an EdgeTX radio, both read their full scale as +-1 by the same rule (hid-layout.ts axisScale, Chrome's Gamepad API normalisation).

The wizard in general: people seldom push a stick quite to its end while setting up; before, 10 % of the simulated people had a stick reading at least 12.8 % too much (p90 0.564) and 72 of 432 radio / 96 of 480 pad people at least one stick over 10 %. After END_SNAP: p90 0.516, 13 / 23 people (the rest stirred below 85 %).

The recognised DJI profile (known-devices.ts) uses the full logical range by design (no stir) and a continuous 2.5 % deadband for its measured rest offsets (1.7 % and 1.2 %), which otherwise read as a slow drift.

Not in the simulator's hands, so the owner can compare: the DJI sticks are shorter than a full-size radio's gimbals (the same rate at a smaller thumb movement feels more sensitive), the DJI throttle springs to the middle (= 50 %), and expo or reduced rates set in his previous radio's EdgeTX model would have softened that radio. Rates (and Quick rates expo) in Settings apply to every controller.
